newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slip but uptrend still strong-brokers.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slip but uptrend still strong-brokers.

text.p: Strong trade in the milling and cement sectors kept the Cairo bourse buzzing on Sunday but failed to keep prices at Thursday's record high.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index slipped 0.04 points to 239.92 points but brokers described the fall as a mere hiccup in the market's uptrend. Volume was an average 17.16 million ($5.05 million).
"Today's slippage is negligible. I expect the market to go up, the fundamentals are right and there's nothing to push it down," said broker Sherief Cararah of Hermes-EFG
Other brokers complained that a new computerised clearing system was still a handicap to trade.

East Delta Flour Mills was the day's most active share, rising 0.99 pounds to 38.25 on talk of higher than forecast profits. Upper Egypt Flour Mills followed suit, gaining 0.40 to 48.25 and Central and West Delta Flour Mills also closed 0.25 pounds higher at 29.25.
Talk of profits revived trading in the blue-chip cement sector, brokers said.

Egyptian Portland Tora Cement rose 2.66 percent to 65.05 pounds on rumours the firm had slashed costs and pumped up production. Slightly higher cement prices also pushed up Suez Cement shares 0.10 pounds to 48.75.
Healthy profit forecasts also buoyed trading in fertiliser firm Egyptian Financial and Industrial and shares closed 5.26 percent higher at 65.01.

The day's biggest gainer was new privatisation General Silos and Storage, rising 12.82 percent to 44.00 pounds in brisk trade. But brokers said the bourse may scrap the transactions because the newly listed firm has yet to give shareholders their stocks.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 358.75 points from Thursday's 359.68 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 169.29 points from 169.08 points.
Advances outnumbered declines 17 to 16, while 26 shares ended unchanged.
